The woman steadies a steel windscreen beside a shallow brazier so a kettle can continue boiling. Test whether real fuel-attached fire, embers, smoke, distinct kettle steam, directional firelight, wet-stone reflection, weather relation and a physically credible gripping action can be read together. Use only the reference face and black bob with bangs. Retain default sensual 1/fetish 0 as subtle natural presence. Inspect actual native pixels and thumbnail; separate baseline success from any postcore fire-data contribution. User acceptance remains pending.

pixel_success_criteria: Flame is rooted in combustible fuel in the brazier, with readable fuel/ember state.
Smoke begins at the fuel and kettle steam begins at the spout; the origins stay visibly distinct.
Glove contacts the windscreen with a plausible visible arm chain and support.
Firelight and wet-rock reflection have the nearby fire as their visible source.
Wind/drizzle, cold shoreline and protected practical kettle fire make one readable situation.
Reference face, black bob and bangs remain apparent while wardrobe and scene are new.
confusion_boundaries: Pale kettle steam is not proof of fire smoke.
Orange wet-rock reflection is not a second source of fire.
Red fuel ember is not a free-standing flame.
Rain streaks are not ember sparks.
A profile exposed or a literal prompt phrase is not pixel evidence or causal proof of data contribution.
